applicability_conditions: Applicable to a representative volume element (RVE) with a mixed-grain microstructure; assumes dislocation density decreases with increasing distance from the grain boundary (based on Guan and Yu, 2017), and rand(i,j,k) is a random variable between 0 and 1 representing deformed microstructure effects.
purpose: Calculates the increment of dislocation density caused by work hardening (WH) for a cell at coordinates (i,j,k) in grain r of the RVE, accounting for grain-size effects and the inhomogeneous distribution of dislocation density with distance from grain boundaries.

symbols.meaning: Increment of dislocation density caused by work hardening (WH) for the cell at coordinates (i,j,k) in grain r, per strain increment
Normalization coefficient used to ensure that the average accumulation of all dislocation density caused by WH equals d\rho_{WH} in each strain increment
Average accumulation of dislocation density caused by work hardening (WH) in each strain increment
Average grain size (AGS) calculated by Eq. (24)
Effect of intense strain localizations brought by different grain sizes in mixed grains on the dislocation density
Number of cells belonging to the grain boundary of grain r
Distance from the cell with coordinates (i,j,k) to the p-th grain boundary in grain r

Random variable representing the influence of deformed microstructure (including microbands and cellular structures) on the distribution of dislocation density; defined as a random variable between 0 and 1

unmapped: The term (1/k_{bd}^{r}) \sum_{p=1}^{k_{bd}^{r}} (L_p^{r}(i,j,k)/L_0)^{-2} represents the distribution of dislocation density in grain r and decreases with increasing distance from the grain boundary.
rand(i,j,k) is defined in reference to the definition of non-uniform stored energy in the Monte Carlo model proposed by Wang et al. (2009).
d_{ave} is the average grain size (AGS) calculated by Eq. (24).
